Package index

The three parts

Every model is these three functions, written as three statements: the world, the tick, the run.

abm_setup()
Set up a model
abm_go()
Declare what happens each tick
abm_run()
Run a model

Declaring the world

The specifications you hand to abm_setup().

abm_agents()
Declare a group of agents
abm_network()
Declare a persistent network between agents

Steps: interaction and matching

Who interacts with whom this tick. Runs first, because the steps below read the pairing it leaves standing.

abm_match()
Match agents into pairs or groups

Steps: updating agents

All five write a value somewhere; the only difference is which row is written. Ordered by reach: the agent itself, the agent itself in a given order, its neighbourhood, one other agent, the whole population.

abm_rules()
Update agent columns
abm_sequential()
Update agent columns one agent at a time
abm_neighbours()
Summarise each agent's neighbourhood
abm_tell()
Write a value into another agent's row
abm_global()
Update a shared, population-level value

Steps: network topology

Changing what is connected to what.

abm_link()
Add edges between matched agents
abm_unlink()
Remove edges between matched agents

Steps: edge data

Attaching a value to edges that already exist, without touching the topology.

abm_draw()
Attach a value to every edge, visible from both ends

Steps: demographics

The only steps that change the size of the population.

abm_birth()
Add agents
abm_death()
Remove agents

Steps: control flow

Replaying a block of the steps above within a single tick.

abm_repeat()
Repeat a block of steps until a condition holds

Working with results

abm_globals()
Global values recorded during a run
abm_edges()
The network at the end of a run
n_agents()
Total number of agents in a model
